title: Utility Commands (util time-ms, util uuid)
description: Implement the two util subcommands. These are stateless, simple commands but they must conform to the JSON output contract.
prerequisiteState: Story 2 complete. IOutputWriter and JsonOutputWriter working.
goal: util time-ms and util uuid produce correct JSON output and exit 0.
scope: Create src/CliqCli/Commands/UtilCommands.cs with TimeMsCommand and UuidCommand
TimeMsCommand: no settings beyond GlobalSettings; ExecuteAsync returns { "status": "ok", "data": { "ts": <DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()> } }
UuidCommand: no settings beyond GlobalSettings; ExecuteAsync returns { "status": "ok", "data": { "uuid": <Guid.NewGuid().ToString()> } }
Register both under 'util' branch in Program.cs
Unit tests: time-ms returns a number > 0 in 'ts'; uuid returns a valid UUID v4 string; both exit 0
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors and 0 warnings
util time-ms returns { "status": "ok", "data": { "ts": <number> } } on stdout, exit 0
util uuid returns { "status": "ok", "data": { "uuid": "<guid>" } } on stdout, exit 0
Both commands work without a configured account
contextForAgent: Simple story. Output must go through IOutputWriter, never Console.Write. The ts field is a Unix millisecond timestamp (long). The uuid field is a lowercase hyphenated UUID v4 string from Guid.NewGuid().ToString().
